signature.name: Spodek
signature.detail: Katowice's most recognizable building, a flying-saucer-shaped arena that has become the symbol of the city and hosts concerts and events. See it from outside at dusk when it is lit up; the surrounding Market Square area is easy to reach on foot or by tram from the center.

signature.name: Silesian Museum
signature.detail: A major museum of regional history and art built on the site of a former coal mine, with striking architecture set into the old shafts. Allow a few hours and check opening days before you go, as museums in Poland often close one day a week.

signature.name: Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial and Museum
signature.detail: The former Nazi concentration camp, a sobering and essential memorial about an hour from Katowice. Book tickets in advance, expect a lot of walking outdoors, and dress respectfully for the site.

signature.name: Legendia (Silesian Amusement Park)
signature.detail: Poland's oldest amusement park, a fun family break from the city's industrial sights. Go on a weekday in summer to avoid queues and check ride schedules before traveling there.

transport: Tram or bus ticket about $1; taxis affordable
